The gap, and where the figures come from
54%

of UK SMEs say they are using AI, up from 35% a year earlier.

6%

of small firms have AI embedded in day-to-day work.

Most firms have adopted AI. Almost none have installed it. The difference is not the tool. It is the fitting: whether the AI lives inside the systems the business runs, reads what it needs to read, writes where it needs to write, and asks a human when it is not sure.

Adopted
  • A ChatGPT seat someone pays for.
  • A prompt found on LinkedIn, used twice.
  • A pilot that stalled in March.
  • The owner still re-keying numbers on a Sunday.
Fitted
  • An agent reconciling Xero before anyone is in.
  • Your written way of working loaded into Claude, so it answers like your best person.
  • Quotes drafted from the last fifty you won.
  • The month-end report on your desk by eight.

    What it does, and what it looks like running
    • 01
      Reconciles bank lines against invoices and bills in Xero.

      Payouts, payments in, direct debits, transfers. In the order your bookkeeper would do it.

    • 02
      Codes recurring spend to rules you set once.

      Telephone, insurance, software, rent. Tell it once; it remembers.

    • 03
      Flags the handful that need a human, with the reason.

      Every match is noted. Nothing is hidden in a black box.

    06The studio

    Not consultants. Wrights.

    A consultant tells you what the ship needs. An agency builds a boat and leaves. A wright fits the thing into the structure you already have, and stays until it holds.

    The name, the people, the numbers
    wrightnoun

    A maker or builder of a particular thing: shipwright, millwright, wheelwright, playwright. From the Old English wryhta, a worker. We took the name because it describes the job.

    Who

    An operator and a builder. One of us has spent a career running a business and knows which hours actually matter. The other builds the tools. Every job gets both.

    Where it started

    Ledgerwright began as an agent built to take Xero reconciliation off a real finance desk. Every tool after it starts the same way: a real job, on a real desk, that we were tired of doing by hand.

    How many

    A small number of businesses at a time. Twenty audits a month, twenty installs, and a handful of fitted jobs. Enough to do it properly.

    The standardWhat we hold ourselves to

    “A wright does not advise on the ship. A wright builds it so it floats.”

    Nothing ships from here that we would not run in our own business. If it is not saving you hours you can count, we have not finished.
